home.heroText: I'm Brais. Developer, maker, geek and professional collector of things I probably shouldn't start. This is where curiosity turns into experiments — and experiments turn into things.
home.featuredText: The first experiment is the place itself: a home for everything I build, learn, break and occasionally finish.
home.hypothesisText: A personal lab is more interesting when it documents attempts, not just achievements.
home.readerText: Can I make reading comics and books feel fundamentally better?
home.learnText: Pick a skill I barely have and make something that forces me to learn it.
home.unknownText: The next experiment is not decided yet. That's part of the fun.
home.manifesto: I like programming. I like comics. I like making things. I like learning. I like telling stories. Instead of turning those interests into ten separate identities, I'm testing what happens when they all feed the same creative practice.
home.aboutTitle: The projects are the point. I'm the weird constant.
home.aboutText: There's a professional story behind all this too: telecommunications, filmmaking, fullstack development, large-scale frontend work and AI systems. It's useful context — just not the headline.
home.videoIntro: Short videos are the front door. The lab is where the rabbit hole starts.
home.communityIntro: I make the final call. But if enough people point at the same shiny object, I'm going to have a very hard time ignoring it.
home.pollQuestion: If you had to choose the next rabbit hole:
home.pollNote: Your choice is remembered on this device. Public voting lives in the lab's community space.
home.suggestionText: Seriously. Weird projects, useful tools, ridiculous experiments. If it can be made, I want to hear it.
home.testTitle: What kind of lab visitor are you?
home.testIntro: Three questions. No data collection. Absolutely no scientific validity. Surprisingly accurate anyway.
home.testQuestion: Pick the answer that feels most like you.
home.followText: Follow an experiment when you care about it. Read the full story, see the failures, grab the files and decide what I should try next. The internet gets enough endless feeds. I want to leave artifacts.
home.counterHint: A tiny homage to the old web. Counts are powered by GoatCounter.

imagine.title: IMAGINE
imagine.headline: Start with the question, not the answer.
imagine.text: A weird thought, a problem I can't stop poking, a sketch on a napkin. This is where the rabbit hole starts.

create.title: CREATE
create.headline: Make the thing before the excuse gets good.
create.text: Prototype it. Print it. Code it. Draw it. Build the smallest real version that can teach me something.

share.title: SHARE
share.headline: Put the process where people can see it.
share.text: The polished result is useful. The mistakes are often more useful. I want both — and I want people to play with them.

repeat.title: REPEAT
repeat.headline: Keep the loop alive.
repeat.text: Learn, steal the lesson, start another experiment. The point isn't to arrive. It's to keep making interesting things.

wildcard.title: Something completely ridiculous
wildcard.text: You decide what the rabbit hole is.

questions.one: You get a free weekend. What happens?
questions.two: What makes you lose track of time?
questions.three: Your prototype is a mess. You…

choices.system: Figure out how it all connects.

builder.title: THE BUILDER
builder.text: You don't need permission. Give you a pile of parts and you'll eventually make a thing out of them.

explorer.title: THE EXPLORER
explorer.text: You are powered by questions. The destination is optional; the rabbit hole is the point.

storyteller.title: THE STORYTELLER
storyteller.text: You make things memorable. You notice the human bit hiding underneath the technical bit.

systems.title: THE SYSTEMS THINKER
systems.text: You can't leave a loose wire alone. You want to understand how the whole machine works.

about.lead: I like making things enough that I stopped trying to separate all the things I like making.
about.copy1: I'm a developer, maker and geek based in Spain. My background started in Telecommunications Engineering, wandered through filmmaking, and eventually landed in software — but the thread through all of it has always been the same: curiosity followed by making.
about.copy2: I build software, play with electronics, 3D printing and servers, make videos, read too many comics and occasionally start projects that are much larger than the amount of free time I have. This site is where those threads meet.

001.title: Make the lab worth visiting.
001.hypothesis: A personal lab is more interesting when it documents attempts, not just achievements.
001.objective: Build a repeatable home for ideas, builds, failures and results — not another polished portfolio.
001.constraint: It has to stay fast, responsive and cheap to host.
001.success: Someone discovers an experiment, gets something useful or entertaining from it, and wants to see what happens next.

002.title: Build a better digital reader.
002.hypothesis: Most digital readers optimise for features. A great reader should optimise for immersion.
002.objective: Prototype a reading engine from scratch and see whether the experience can feel closer to owning the book.
002.constraint: Start small. Web first. No giant platform before the first good reading session.
002.success: A comic or book feels so good to read that the interface gets out of the way.

003.title: Learn by building the thing.
003.hypothesis: Real constraints create better learning than passive study.
003.objective: Pick an unfamiliar skill and ship one small, finished artifact with it.
003.constraint: No waiting until I'm good enough. The artifact is the curriculum.
003.success: A finished thing, a visible before/after and an honest account of what actually accelerated learning.
